Jezero Go/No-Go

A recording of the planner's guided tour: a time cut, the point of no return, your own sites, and a decision made halfway out.

Recorded from
The live planner
Terrain
MRO CTX elevation, 20 m
Images
Perseverance Mastcam-Z
Transcript

Plan a walk across real Mars terrain. With a 160-minute budget, the west fan in Jezero Crater fits the time limit: GO, 141 minutes against a 150-minute safe return. Mission Control cuts 30 minutes. Now it's NO-GO, and the chart marks the point where the crew must turn back. The best plan that still fits swaps to the closer crater floor.

Add your own site anywhere on the chart and give it a science value. Add the west fan as well and the plan overruns the limit. "Best plan" picks the most valuable set of sites that still gets the crew home in time.

Now run the EVA. The crew sets out for the west fan, and Mission Control cuts the clock mid-walk. The planner offers three choices from where the crew stands: continue (NO-GO), re-plan to the crater floor (GO), or turn back now. The crew re-plans and comes home safe with science collected.

Routes use the USGS Mars 2020 CTX elevation model from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, at 20 m per cell. Walking speed depends on slope. Rover images are from Perseverance Mastcam-Z. Habitat and site positions, and the walking model, are simulation assumptions.
